hook: Women at home: lower for 3 seconds.
spoken: Women at home: lower for 3 seconds. Fast reps let momentum do the work. Count it out loud: one, two, three, up. Muscles stay in charge. Which rep do you rush? Save this, then tell me.

hook: Myth: slow reps are only for beginners.
spoken: Myth: slow reps are only for beginners. Try a slow glute bridge on the floor. Rise for 2 counts. Lower for 3. Slow is not easy. Slow is control. Slow rep or fast rep? Tell me below.

why: It calls out a belief many women hold, so viewers stay to see whether the myth holds up.

beats: with a mirror at your side.
Pain? Stop and ask a pro.
spoken: Knees wobbling mid-squat? Slow down. Rushing hides the wobble. Slow shows it. Lower for 3 counts with a mirror at your side. Spot it. Adjust. Repeat. Pain? Stop and ask a pro. Where do you wobble? Save this for leg day.

why: It names a pain the viewer can see in her own squat and gives the fix straight away.

hook: Women at home: stop bouncing at the bottom.
spoken: Women at home: stop bouncing at the bottom. The bounce skips the hard part. Pause one full second at the bottom. Then rise. Discipline creates freedom. Do you bounce? Be honest. Send this to a friend.

why: It names one exact mistake that viewers can spot in their own reps, and the one-second pause is easy to try right away.

hook: Don't add more reps today. Slow them down.
spoken: Don't add more reps today. Slow them down. Take 3 counts down. Take 1 count up. Same reps. Much more control. Hips sag? Stop there. That is your limit today. How many clean reps did you get? Comment it.

why: It tells viewers to do the opposite of what they expect (fewer reps, not more), which breaks the scroll pattern.

hook: Women who rush squats: grab a chair.
spoken: Women who rush squats: grab a chair. Touch the seat lightly, never drop onto it. Take 3 counts to get there. Then stand tall. Chair is a guide, not a rest stop. Chair squats: easy or hard? Save this and tell me.
